features.note: Frame 0 shows facade signage, generic display blocks, room numbers, and circulation markings, but frame 1 loses most of that surface context instead of preserving the plan while only cycling content.

Aisle lines and abstract screen content read in frame 0, but acoustic-panel rhythm is sparse and the frame-1 auditorium evidence collapses to a mostly black-and-white image without coherent aisle or wall detail.
Abstract menu panels are present, but POS, snack-machine, and wayfinding cues remain weak rectangular placeholders, and the second concessions frame obscures the surrounding front-of-house context.

UG67 is readable in its close preset, but most in-building IDs and terminal cues are too small in the complete-network view; dense crossings, detached-looking blue segments, and inconsistent arrow visibility make direction and endpoint association ambiguous.

The labels-off corridor proves suppression, but the labels-on engineering view is crowded and many labels are unreadable; frame-1 architecture captures do not preserve coherent geometry and surface context across the state pair.

important_features.note: People, doors, and counters generally retain plausible relative scale, while small devices depend heavily on oversized labels and remain difficult to identify in wide presets.
Red commercial accents and dark auditorium zones are distinguishable in frame 0, but frame-1 captures flatten into clipped black and white regions that erase the intended hierarchy.
Green trunks are visible, but several blue media segments read as floating fragments and dense line crossings obscure terminal-to-route containment.

defects: The frame-1 concessions, corridor, and Sala 3 captures replace most surrounding geometry and surface shading with large black or white regions, so the required content cycle is not visually coherent across states.
Most internal endpoint labels in the complete-network preset are too small or blurred to read, and multiple labels and routes compete in the same screen space.
Blue network segments in the UG67 and complete-network views appear detached or floating, while dense crossings and sparse arrowheads make route direction ambiguous.
Front-of-house POS, snack-machine, and wayfinding cues read as generic flat rectangles rather than distinct operational surface details.
Acoustic panel rhythm is sparse, and the frame-1 auditorium captures omit the aisle, panel, door-number, and carpet context visible in frame 0.
The grazing-details view is too wide and front-biased to expose meso surface relief or close material/detail continuity.
corrections: Stabilize every frame-1 capture so poster_frame/display_frame changes only the abstract poster, menu, and screen content while preserving the exact frame-0 geometry, materials, exposure, and camera.

Recompose the complete-network and UG67 presets with readable in-building IDs, collision-free label placement, consistent high-contrast backplates, and clearly aligned direction arrows at every visible route.
Remove detached-looking blue route fragments and resolve visible route crossings so each media segment reads as a continuous endpoint-to-endpoint path.
Replace placeholder front-of-house rectangles with distinct generated POS faces, snack-machine controls, menu groupings, and concise wayfinding that remain readable in both deterministic frames.
Carry acoustic-panel rhythm, aisle/carpet markings, room numbers, and evacuation cues through both auditorium frames, then capture a genuinely close grazing view that exposes their meso relief.
